messages.subject: MCMC efficient sampling
parts:
Hi,


I am trying to use the efficient sampling feature of Stan (NUTS/HMC) instead of using Metropolis-Hasting MCMC for estimating small failure probabilities in high dimensions.


Is it possible to employ just the sampling technique of Stan directly? Is there any function in Stan for that to use it with Matlab or R? (I have the target distribution and the Initial state for the Markov Chain)


I went through the examples in Stan’s guideline but most of them are talking about Bayesian inference and fitting data to the models.


I need to work on those samples for estimating small failure probabilities.


I would appreciate it if you could guide me in this regard.

Thank you,

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] MCMC efficient sampling
parts:
There are R and MATLAB interfaces to Stan (see mc-stan.org under Interfaces
tab).

There's no requirement that the density from which Stan samples
be a Bayesian posterior. You can write down any old density you
want and Stan will sample from it. It's just that we usually condition
on data as well as constants, giving us a Bayesian posterior.

If you said more about the density you want to sample from, we could
say more.

- Bob

P.S. Thanks for writing to the list.

parts:
> On Feb 27, 2017, at 8:35 PM, Hamed Nikbakht <hamednik...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I'm so sorry for my previous message. I worked on that and i think finally i figured it out. but now i have another issue.
Glad to see you got it running.
> I want to have 10 iterations but it just save 5 iterations. where's my mistake?

It's an unfortunate choice of output messages.

By default, Stan splits the iterations in half and does warmup for the
first half. By default, it looks like StataStan's not saving the warmup
iterations. So you only see the 5 sampling iterations. The misleading thing
is that it says zero warmup iterations, when there are actually 5 warmup
iterations---the just don't get saved to file, so they're not visible to
the posterior analysis package here.

> load('Ufile.mat');
> N = length(ux);
> MCMC_dat = struct('N',N);
> initial = struct('x',ux');
> fit = stan('file','MC.stan','data',MCMC_dat,'chains',1,'iter',10,'init',initial,'algorithm','NUTS','sample_file','output-6.csv');
> %print(fit)
>
> Showing part of the results where it shows just 5 iterations has been saved:

>
> >> print(fit)
> Inference for Stan model: MC_model
> 1 chains: each with iter=(5); warmup=(0); thin=(1); 5 iterations saved.
> Warmup took (0.0070) seconds, 0.0070 seconds total
> Sampling took (0.011) seconds, 0.011 seconds total
> Mean MCSE StdDev 5% 50% 95% N_Eff N_Eff/s R_hat
> lp__ -4.9e+002 3.1 6.9 -4.9e+002 -4.9e+002 -4.8e+002 5.0 455 9.9e-001
> accept_stat__ 7.2e-001 0.073 0.16 6.0e-001 6.5e-001 1.0e+000 5.0 455 9.2e-001
> .
> .
> .
> .
> .
> I have another question. I want to make sure whether I'm on the right track.
> (my problem's dimension is 1000 and my target distribution is a standard normal distribution and I have a vector x (size 1000x1) which i set it as the initial values of my problem for the HMC NUTS sampling.
> since, I want to have 10 sample from each dimension, i set the iteration as 10)

Unless you generate them with the _rng functions in generated quantities, 10
iterations won't give you the equivalent of 10 independent draws. You have to
go longer and thin because there's correlation.

Also, you don't need to initialize for most problems.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] MCMC efficient sampling
parts:
Sounds like you have an older version of the manual. We're
using normal_lpdf(y | mu, sigma) as the notation now. We
still support normal_log(y, mu, sigma), but that will go away
along with other deprecated features in Stan 3.

And I also see you're using MatlabStan. Don't know much
about that, either, but it also uses CmdStan to do the sampling.

- Bob
